title: Bisecting a broken graph: previews are your print statement
hook: Something is wrong and nothing errors. Put a preview in the middle and throw away half the graph. Four previews find one bad node out of sixteen.

verified.claim: PreviewAny is an output node. It prints strings and numbers as they are, tries JSON, then falls back to str.
Real PreviewAny output for a small image was tensor text with its values, and for a latent a dict with samples and downscale_ratio_spacial.
With torch's default summary, one NaN in the middle of a 64 by 64 latent doesn't show in the text, and a corner one does.
verified.ref: same settings as PreviewAny, in the lab and in a real process

verified.claim: The graph f_bisect_probes ran on a CPU.
Core has PreviewImage, MaskPreview, GetImageSize, GetLatentSize and SaveLatent.
The server accepts partial_execution_targets to run only chosen outputs.

unchecked: Halving assumes a chain. A graph with branches needs judgement about where 'the middle' is, and we have no measure for that.
How the editor offers a partial run isn't tested here.
